papers.title: Deformation mechanisms and compressive response of NbTaTiZr alloy via machine learning potentials
papers.abstract: Refractory multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) are key research focus for excellent high-temp properties and engineering potential. Deformation mechanisms/mechanical behaviors of quaternary NbTaTiZr MPEA under high strain rates/extreme temps remain unclear. We built a variable-composition ML potential for NbTaTiZr, combined with MD simulations to study effects of crystal orientation, strain rate, temp, composition on compressive mechanics. NbTaTiZr shows structural/mechanical anisotropy in compression [111] max yield strength, [110] min (prone to twinning), [100] via local disorder/dislocation slip (dominant 1/2<111> dislocations). At 10^10 s^-1, yield strength rises sharply, disordered structures increase; high strain rates suppress dislocations to promote disordering. Retains high strength at 2100 K. Higher Nb/Ta boosts yield strength, Ti/Zr reduce it. Reveals MPEA mechanical anisotropy and strain-rate-dependent disordering, guiding high-performance refractory alloy design.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the deformation mechanisms and compressive response of the refractory NbTaTiZr multi-principal element alloy under high strain rates and extreme temperatures.
summary_en.method: A variable-composition machine learning potential was developed and combined with molecular dynamics simulations to study the effects of crystal orientation, strain rate, temperature, and composition on compressive mechanical behavior.
summary_en.result: The alloy exhibits structural and mechanical anisotropy; high strain rates suppress dislocation activity and promote disordering, while high strength is retained up to 2100 K.
summary_en.validation: The study relies entirely on molecular dynamics simulations without experimental validation.
